title: Dallas Fed Trimmed Mean PCE (Aug 2026 data) — the first trimmed mean computed off BEA's revised components
source: EST: dallasfed.org/research/pce fetched direct 2026-09-15 (carrying July 2026 data — 1-month 2.2%, 6-month 2.3%, 12-month 2.3%) states its next release date as September 30 and states verbatim that "Updates to the Trimmed Mean PCE Inflation Rate follow BEA's release schedule for Personal Income and Outlays data". The paired leg was re-fetched the same day: bea.gov/news/schedule lists verbatim "Personal Income and Outlays, August 2026" at 8:30 AM on September 30, alongside "GDP (Third Estimate), Industries, Corporate Profits, State GDP, and State Personal Income, 2nd Quarter 2026; State PCE, 2025". Two primaries agree and there is no date doubt. Stays `estimate` on one mechanical count instead: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy defines `FED:` narrowly as "federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar" and has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank research release — the same taxonomy gap jgb-20y-auction-2026-09-15, ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and boj-decision-2026-09-18 each recorded for a non-US sovereign debt office and a foreign central bank. Verified at both primaries 2026-09-15
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial-research lane 2026-09-15 (D-15), superseding proposals/dallas-fed-trimmed-mean-2026-09-30.from-pce-2026-09-30.json, which is read and inert. WHAT THIS RELEASE IS: at the same 08:30 ET minute as pce-2026-09-30, the Dallas Fed republishes the trimmed mean computed off BEA's newly revised components AND restates its own 2021-2026 history, because BEA's 2026 annual update re-deflates portfolio management and investment advice, legal services, and computer software across 2021Q1-2026Q1. WHY IT IS A ROW OF ITS OWN: the restated history makes a difference-of-differences computable within minutes of the release — the revision's effect on July-2026 core y/y against its effect on the July-2026 12-month trimmed mean, same reference month, free of any August news — which is the direct measurement pce-2026-09-30's standing kill switch ("a published estimate of the revision's effect on trimmed mean appears") has been waiting for; two searches on 2026-09-15 found no such estimate published anywhere, so that switch is still unfired and self-resolves here. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE REVISION: measured this session from FRED (PCETRIM12M159SFRBDAL + PCEPILFE, 583 monthly observations 1978-01 to 2026-07), the core-minus-trimmed-mean wedge is 1.06pp in July 2026 — the 95.7th percentile of 48 years, with only 30 months at or above 1.00pp and those in three clusters: 1980-83, 2021-22, and now 2026-05 onward. Over thirteen months the wedge went 0.11pp -> 1.06pp while the trimmed mean FELL (2.70% -> 2.28%) and core ROSE (2.81% -> 3.34%). The gauge Chair Warsh has stated he prefers reads near target while the gauge the mandate is written against reads above 3%, and the Dallas Fed itself published two 2026 papers saying this is the configuration in which its own measure under-reads (2026-04-16 on positive skewness; 2026-08-13 on a recalibrated alternative reading 2.6% against the official 2.2% for the 12 months ended June). Impact `medium`, not `high`: it publishes into the same minute as the PCE print, the GDP third estimate, ADP and the advance economic indicators, inside a 47-event quarter-end corridor also carrying the government funding deadline, so its own tape contribution is unattributable; the value is informational. `symbols: []` — no house playbook is macro-keyed to it and nothing here licenses a position.
